transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Liam (Ember SecOps), Sofia (Eng Dir), Kenji (SRE)

Summary:
Quick triage of Ember's recent 3rd-party pen test. Review of critical/medium/low findings, discussion of patch cadence and secure SDLC adjustments, mapping vulnerabilities to owners, and alignment on audit log exports, KMS usage, and SOC2 evidence. Agreed to produce an annotated remediation plan, share logs and schedule a follow-up.

Topics covered:
- Pen test results overview (3rd-party, conducted 2025-10-20)
- Immediate critical/medium findings and repro notes
- Patch cadence: current 90-day vs recommended 30/60-day windows
- Secure SDLC: SCA, SAST, dependency pinning, PR gating
- RBAC/SSO: review of admin role coverage and session length
- Audit logs and retention policy, log export format (json vs syslog)
- Encryption & KMS: envelope crypto, HSM usage, key rotation cadence
- Data residency: EU logs, US compute, hybrid concerns

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay, um, thanks for joining everyone. I think we'll try to keep to about an hour and make sure we leave time for the remediation plan.
00:12 Liam: yeah, appreciate it. We've got the pentest results in hand, a mix of auth issues and a couple of dependency CVEs that popped up.
00:20 Carlos: cool, can you remind us which vendor did the test and the scope?
00:25 Liam: it was RedShield Labs — scope was public API surface, internal admin console, and one of our private connectors to S3 buckets. We opted out of on-prem agents.
00:38 Priya: thanks. from the summary you sent there was one high severity that the vendor labeled as "elevated auth bypass" — can we run through that first?
00:46 Sofia: yes, that's the one. Quick context, we use SAML SSO via Okta, and our admin panel RBAC has a legacy endpoint that was missed in recent refactors. The vendor exploited a parameter tamper that let them escalate to admin for one session.
01:02 Carlos: uh, got it. is that reproducible in prod or only in the staging harness?
01:08 Sofia: they've reproduced it against a staging snapshot but believe it also exists in prod without exploit chaining.
01:15 Maya: ok, so immediate mitigation — we recommend invalidating active sessions and rotating SAML certs, and adding an emergency WAF rule to block the tampered param while a code fix is deployed.
01:28 Kenji: can WAF be applied fast enough? we have a 3-hour change freeze in peak window, but out of window we can push.
01:34 Liam: our patch window is Tue 02:00–04:00 UTC typically; we can make an exception for critical fixes.
01:40 Priya: note for SOC2 evidence, make sure you capture session invalidation and timeline — that'll help the audit trail.
01:48 Carlos: on the dependency CVEs — two were medium severity in a transitive JS package, one is a critical native lib on the S3 connector. vendor provided PoC for the native lib.
02:00 Sofia: the native lib is tricky, it's pinned by another internal package; we've been on a 90-day bump cadence which slowed us. We've been discussing moving to a 30/60-day cadence for high-risk components.
02:12 Maya: that's a common tradeoff. from Redwood's side we can provide a CVE export from the node agents and tag vulnerable instances for you, plus a suggested prioritization matrix.
02:22 Liam: can Redwood show us the audit log around the S3 connector? we want to validate the calls the pentester used.
02:28 Carlos: yes, we can export the audit log with request/response metadata, timestamps, and the KV cache keys redacted. we'll send a sample JSON export.
02:40 Sofia: what's your retention window by default? we need 1 year in EU and 2 years for certain logs.
02:46 Priya: default hosted retention is 90 days, but for Private customers we support longer retention and you can push logs to your SIEM. We'll include the retention config options in the doc.
02:58 Kenji: on KMS, vendor flagged that a service account had direct access to unwrapped keys in staging. we do use a cloud KMS but the access boundary is wide.
03:08 Carlos: we recommend envelope encryption and ensuring service accounts have encrypt-only IAM roles, not decrypt. also rotate keys every 90 days; we support AWS KMS and bring-your-own HSM.
03:22 Sofia: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK)?
03:25 Priya: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer CMK via AWS but can integrate with customer keys for enterprise.
03:34 Liam: any suggestions re: key rotation if we have a lot of short-lived sessions?
03:38 Carlos: rotate the wrapping keys on a schedule, not per session. session keys can be ephemeral and rotate at the app layer — avoid decrypt perms for service accounts.
03:48 Maya: circling back to secure SDLC — vendor called out lack of SAST gating on some repos, and outdated dependency pinning in the connector repo.
03:56 Sofia: we only started SAST last quarter, some repos still on our old CI.
04:02 Priya: action: put SAST gates for high-risk repos and require dependency scanning on PR. that will help in SOC2 and ISO 27001 scope.
04:12 Liam: for the high finding — we accept the vendor severity but want to ensure remediation doesn't break integrations. can Redwood run a pre-production smoke test against a staging snapshot?
04:21 Carlos: yes, we can run regression harnesses and also suggest canary rollout steps via the console: traffic-splitting and automated fallback to previous model. (note: slight audio glitch)
04:34 Kenji: we need concrete timelines. if we push the fix in two weeks, what's required from our side?
04:40 Maya: from Redwood: patch plan doc, test creds, sample logs, and access to a staging instance. From Ember: patch window confirmation, code owner, and acceptance criteria.
04:50 Sofia: we'll assign code owners and share timeline today.
04:55 Liam: two other minor notes — vendor suggested better session logging (capture user agent, IP, session ID) and to shorten admin session TTLs.
05:06 Carlos: doable. the console currently stores session metadata; we can add additional fields and expose them in the audit export.
05:14 Priya: also for SOC2, capture proof of RBAC reviews and minute-by-minute audit trails.
05:21 Maya: last, data residency — you mentioned EU logs should remain within eu-central, right?
05:26 Sofia: yes, EU logs for EU customers. compute can be US for now but logs must stay.
05:33 Carlos: we can configure region-based retention and log routing; we'll include the config snippet.
05:42 Maya: ok, wrap up — action items listed, we'll produce the annotated pen test report with remediation guidance and timeline. follow-up meeting proposed week of Nov 10.
05:54 Liam: sounds good. thanks everyone.
06:00 End of transcript.
